extraction.Name: James Pulliam
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent to his 160 acre allotment, when it was issued in 1919, for he did not desire to have taxes to pay; but the Indian Agency, at Pine Ridge, advised him that the land would be assessed for taxes at any rate, and later sold for same; so he accepted the patent
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: the place being behind for taxes, was put up and sold for the taxes
extraction.Buyer: deponent thinks that Barker bought it
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: the place being behind for taxes, was put up and sold for the taxes
extraction.Occupation/Income: drives a dray in Crawford, Nebraska, and works at any common labor he can get either in town or the country for his living; has some land on which he raises stock; and that this labor and the stock on his ranch is the source of all his income
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent, has good health; has a wife and three children to support, who have good health; borrowed $65.00 in 1921 from A.R. Barker of Denby, South Dakota — Barker drew up a mortgage on the strength of this loan against his allotment but deponent refused to sign it; deponent asked Barker $1500.00 for the place but Barker said that was too much; Barker urged deponent to sign the mortgage which he again promptly refused to do; deponent considers the place a total loss to him; never sold the place for debts incurred before receiving the patent in fee; never received any help from the County, State nor the United States Government; affidavit sworn December 17, 1928, Shannon County, South Dakota
